units.title: From logits to an output contract
units.outcome: Explain why fluent generation and valid JSON do not establish factual correctness.

units.title: Sampling experiments and reasoning reliability
units.outcome: Design controlled tests for reasoning, positional sensitivity, and model capability boundaries.

units.title: Error analysis before a metric
units.outcome: Turn raw failures into a versioned taxonomy and a frozen evaluation set.

units.title: Exact, semantic, functional, and pairwise evaluation
units.outcome: Choose a metric that matches the task instead of reducing all quality to similarity.

units.title: Calibrate a judge; quantify uncertainty
units.outcome: Measure judge disagreement, order effects, and uncertainty without presenting scores as ground truth.

units.title: Cost, tail latency, and model selection
units.outcome: Build a capacity and cost argument for 500,000 monthly requests using measured quality.

units.title: Package the evaluation contract
units.outcome: Make the first project artifact reproducible before adding retrieval.

units.title: Ingest evidence with provenance
units.outcome: Preserve source structure and access scope before building an index.

units.title: Lexical, dense, and approximate search
units.outcome: Explain the different errors of BM25, embedding geometry, and HNSW.

units.title: Eight chunking strategies and evidence boundaries
units.outcome: Compare fixed, structural, semantic, and hierarchical units under equal budgets.

units.title: Hybrid fusion, reranking, and filters
units.outcome: Keep candidate recall, rank fusion, and final context selection distinct.

units.title: Query expansion and multi-hop retrieval
units.outcome: Use query transformations without laundering generated hypotheses into evidence.

units.title: Context as a budgeted working set
units.outcome: Allocate tokens across policy, evidence, memory, and output while preserving trust.

units.title: Document trees, long context, and the six-condition study
units.outcome: Complete a fair four-family comparison with six required configurations.

units.title: Who controls the next step?
units.outcome: Distinguish a workflow from an agent and select the simplest adequate control flow.

units.title: Build a bounded ReAct loop
units.outcome: Separate model proposals, runtime state, observations, and termination.

units.title: Tool contracts, effects, and unknown outcomes
units.outcome: Make retries safe with validation, stable effect identity, and reconciliation.

units.title: MCP host, client, and server boundaries
units.outcome: Trace initialization, capability discovery, and a tool invocation across distinct responsibilities.

units.title: Implement and test an MCP connection
units.outcome: Choose stdio or StreamableHTTP and enforce real access boundaries.

units.title: State, memory, and framework equivalence
units.outcome: Port the scratch runtime without changing its invariants.

units.title: A runnable and observable research service
units.outcome: Introduce API, trace, and deployment basics before the Project 1 defense.

units.title: Plans as dependency graphs
units.outcome: Define executable tasks with prerequisites, evidence needs, and bounded replanning.

units.title: Planner–executor–verifier contracts
units.outcome: Prevent a polished report from hiding unsupported intermediate claims.

units.title: Six multi-agent arrangements
units.outcome: Choose topology by information flow and responsibility, not role names.

units.title: Coordination failure and recovery
units.outcome: Diagnose deadlocks, disagreement, duplicate work, and context contamination.

units.title: Compare architectures under equal budgets
units.outcome: Separate decomposition gains from extra compute and favorable examples.

units.title: Project 1 release and technical defense
units.outcome: Demonstrate a reproducible evidence-first research platform with its limits.

units.title: Evaluate trajectories and components
units.outcome: Locate the earliest actionable failure inside an agent run.

units.title: Threat-model untrusted instructions
units.outcome: Trace prompt injection from documents, tools, memory, and plans to privileged effects.

units.title: Enforce permissions outside the model
units.outcome: Implement scoped tools, destination controls, secret isolation, and bound approvals.

units.title: Run a reproducible red-team matrix
units.outcome: Measure attack success and defense cost on at least 50 attacks.

units.title: Incident analysis and regression repair
units.outcome: Turn one failure into a testable explanation and a release gate.

units.title: Customer data and synthetic policy fixtures
units.outcome: Start Project 2 without inventing consent or causal business outcomes.

units.title: Diagnose the adaptation problem
units.outcome: Separate missing knowledge, inconsistent behavior, and serving capacity before choosing a technique.

units.title: Dataset engineering for adaptation
units.outcome: Create clean, covered, leak-resistant training and evaluation data.

units.title: SFT, LoRA, QLoRA, and forgetting
units.outcome: Explain what is trained, what is quantized, and where memory is spent.

units.title: The required six-way adaptation study
units.outcome: Compare all six conditions without building six unrelated projects.

units.title: Prefill, decode, and KV-cache accounting
units.outcome: Explain latency and memory using the actual request lifecycle.

units.title: Continuous batching and serving optimization
units.outcome: Benchmark one optimization while preserving quality and latency constraints.

units.title: Capacity at 100 requests per second
units.outcome: Defend a target with workload assumptions, measured capacity, and explicit uncertainty.

units.title: Production request and data boundaries
units.outcome: Connect gateway, cache, queue, database, worker, and fallback.

units.title: Events, checkpoints, and durable execution
units.outcome: Design restartable state transitions for long-running work.

units.title: Outbox, idempotency, and compensation
units.outcome: Handle the crash between external effect and local acknowledgement.

units.title: OpenTelemetry across asynchronous work
units.outcome: Use logs, metrics, traces, span links, and redaction to debug a real failure.

units.title: SLIs, SLOs, canaries, and rollback
units.outcome: Turn measurements into explicit release and operational decisions.

units.title: Run the recovery drill
units.outcome: Demonstrate restart, duplicate delivery, dependency failure, and approval safety.

units.title: Reliability under overload and dependency failure
units.outcome: Combine timeouts, circuit breakers, fallback, load shedding, and error budgets.

units.title: Economics per successful task
units.outcome: Compare routing, caching, compression, and local/hosted serving under quality constraints.

units.title: Close the telemetry-to-evaluation loop
units.outcome: Turn observed failures into labeled cases and controlled releases.

units.title: The final chaos and evaluation matrix
units.outcome: Complete 150 customer scenarios plus explicit fault and attack evidence.

units.title: Report, demo, and architecture defense
units.outcome: Connect business value, implementation, and measured limitations in a 10–15 page report.

units.title: Reproduce, review, and hand over
units.outcome: Prove that another engineer can run the system and understand unresolved risks.
